findings.title: The handover says the Compose half of the backup sequence runs on the orchestrator's host and 'is recorded there', but no Compose backup run exists in any evidence, and DO-D11 changed that Compose sequence (root backup service, '--user 0:0' copy-out, create_host_path: false) without it being run
findings.reproduction: On the frozen candidate (sha256:33266ccd…, source 152db5b5): read docs/handover/backup-restore.md l.76 ('The Compose sequence runs on the orchestrator's host (D-243 Q1). Its result is recorded there, not here.'), l.202 ('The Compose half runs on the orchestrator's host and is recorded there: the backup profile on postgres:18, a second Compose project with new volumes, and /readyz over HTTP.') and l.217 (§10, 'has not been run here … It runs on the orchestrator's host'), and known-limitations.md §5 ('D-256 | The container half of the backup and restore drill (A19) is the orchestrator's host run.'). Then search the orchestrator's host evidence: grep -rl -e '--profile backup' -e 'phase finish' docs/delivery/test-evidence docs/delivery/decisions.md docs/delivery/progress.md finds only a code-security round-1 reviewer repro; host-run.log, host-run-3b.log and host-run-3c.log (steps 00-11, b01-b07) contain no backup step; prefreeze-rg2 has none; the old branch 1612f85fc has no orchestrator backup run either. D-267 (the container host run) lists build, bundle, up/readyz, no-egress smoke and Keycloak, not A19. The DO-D11 handback §4 item 1-2 says the changed Compose sequence was not run and 'The orchestrator's Compose run should confirm step 2'; no decision or evidence of round 2 records that run.
findings.expected: The handover IT inherits states truthfully what has and has not been executed (agent protocol honesty rules: no planned item labelled as done; never report a check as passed that did not run). Either the Compose sequence of backup-restore.md §3.2 (backup profile on postgres:18, the '--user 0:0' copy-out, --phase finish, create_host_path: false refusing an unset MTH_BACKUP_ROOT) and the Compose restore are run on the orchestrator's host and recorded in the evidence, or backup-restore.md (l.76, l.202, §10) and known-limitations.md say plainly that the Compose half has not been run in this release and that only the container-free scripts are tested.
findings.actual: No Compose backup or restore run exists in the candidate's evidence or in the old branch's orchestrator evidence, yet the handover twice says its result 'is recorded there'. DO-D11 then changed the Compose procedure materially (the copy-out now runs the app image as root; the bind mount syntax and its refusal behaviour are new) and asked for an orchestrator Compose run that did not happen. The scripts themselves are sound: in my run on a disposable PostgreSQL backup-restore.test.mjs gives 13/13 (T-E10..T-E12 included), and REQ-S19-012/S20-019's A19 acceptance is met by the container-free drill (DO-F drill and the QA A19 harness). The defect is the false 'recorded there' evidence claim in a handover document plus an untested change to the operator procedure IT will run first; its effect is bounded (documentation and a first-use risk), so Medium, not High.

history.note: Raised by domain-reviewer in DG7 round 2 on candidate sha256:33266ccd…. Repair options: run and record the Compose backup/restore sequence on the orchestrator's host (D-243 Q1), or correct backup-restore.md l.76, l.202 and §10 and the known-limitations D-256 line to say the Compose half was not run in this release.

findings.title: ADR-0063 §1.2 (S3 i18n-key exception) and ADR-0066 §4 (backup-time checks) were not amended for the DO-D11 behaviour changes (narrower isI18nKey rule; new ownerOnly check and refused shared root)
findings.reproduction: Read docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0063-…md l.82: the S3 row still exempts 'an i18n key ([a-z0-9_.]+)'. tools/release/secret-scan.mjs now uses isI18nKey (needs a separator, segments ≤20 chars and ≤3 digits). Read ADR-0066-…md §4: the set fails 'unless all hold' items 1-5; backup.sh now also fails the set on the ownerOnly check and refuses a group/other-writable root (exit 2). DO-D11 handback §5 open questions 1 and 2 ask the solution-architect for these amendments; D-282 does not answer them.
findings.expected: The ADRs state the rules as built (p7-work-split §2 rule 2, the rule F-DG7-1002 was repaired under).
findings.actual: The ADR texts are now broader (ADR-0063) or incomplete (ADR-0066 §4) relative to the code. The IT-facing handover is correct (security-controls.md SC-13 and backup-restore.md §3.3 describe the new rules), so there is no behavioural effect. Documentation drift only; proposed for acceptance as an observation or a dated amendment.
